The failing test `testLang882` is testing the `LookupTranslator` class from `org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate`. The test creates a `LookupTranslator` object with a `CharSequence` array containing `StringBuffer` objects, attempts to translate a `StringBuffer` input, and then asserts the result.

The current bug report mentions that `LookupTranslator` accepts `CharSequence` as input but fails to work with implementations other than `String`. Looking at the implementation of `LookupTranslator.translate`, we can see that it uses `CharSequence.subSequence` to extract a subsequence from the input. However, the bug report indicates that comparing `CharSequence` objects may lead to undefined behavior if implemented by different classes.

The `LookupTranslator` constructor initializes a `HashMap<CharSequence, CharSequence>` named `lookupMap` to store the translation mappings. The `lookupMap` is populated with the provided `CharSequence` array passed to the constructor, but the subsequence extraction in `translate` may encounter issues when comparing different `CharSequence` implementations.

To address the bug where `LookupTranslator` fails to work with `CharSequence` implementations other than `String`, a possible fix could involve converting all input `CharSequence` objects to a consistent implementation (e.g., `String`) before performing comparisons in `translate`.

Next, I will provide the locations of where the fix can be applied.
```
org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.LookupTranslator.translate(java.lang.CharSequence, int, java.io.Writer)
org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.LookupTranslator.LookupTranslator(java.lang.CharSequence[]...)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
